chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Washa from Ahmad ibn A'iz from Abu Khadeejah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

Zarih Al-Muharibi asked him (peace be upon him) about the owned slave who takes the found property. He (peace be upon him) said: 'And what is it to do with the owned slave to the found property? He does not own anything for himself, so the owned slave must not have bothered about it. Thus, it would be befitting for him that he advertises it for a year, so if its seeker comes over, he should hand it over to him, or else it would be in his wealth. So if he dies, it would be an inheritance for his children, and for the one who inherits him. So if a seeker does not come for it, it would be in their wealth. It would be for them; and if its seeker comes over, they should hand it over to him'.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a slave who finds lost property?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a slave's limited autonomy over his person extends to his right of ownership, allowing him to acquire found property (luqata) as personal wealth. The ruling mandates a one-year period of advertisement to locate the original owner; if no claimant appears, the item becomes the slave's permanent asset and part of his inheritance, reflecting the Shia juristic view of a slave's partial financial independence.
